instruction: I have developed a Chrome extension packaged in a zip file on my Desktop. Please install it into Chrome and make sure it is enabled.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Task requires installing an unpacked Chrome extension and ensuring it is enabled. Custom getter reads Chrome Preferences file to extract extension state (state=1 means enabled). Metric checks if 'Hello Extensions' is in the enabled extensions map with value true.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: extension installation AND enabled status
Getter logic correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts extension state (state=1 means enabled) from the correct path
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict (uses expected.get('extension_name') directly, not expected.get('rules'))
Metric checks both existence (extension_name in result) AND enabled status (result[extension_name] == true) before returning 1.0
Expected value 'Hello Extensions' matches the actual extension name from setup configuration
Data flow is semantically correct: user installs extension → Chrome Preferences file updated → getter extraction → metric comparison
State accessibility is correct: Preferences file persists on disk after task completion, no UI dialog needs to be reopened
Postconfig sleep(2) is appropriate to ensure Chrome has written the Preferences file to disk
Rule validation warning about UI/state dependency is a false positive - getter reads from persistent file, not transient UI state
